taxpayer.notes: Medical assistant; lived with her three children and their father, to whom she was not married. State of residence not stated.

adjustments: disallowed qualifying child dependency exemptions, child tax credit and EIC (in part)
disallowed head of household filing status for 2015 and 2016
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Head of household status for 2015 and 2016; $1,000 education credit for 2014
conceded: Respondent conceded the section 6662(a) accuracy-related penalties for all years
Respondent conceded petitioner may claim two of her three children as qualifying child dependents for personal exemptions, child tax credit and EIC for 2014, 2015 and 2016

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner lived with her three children and their father during 2014-2016
findings_of_fact.snippet: She lived with her three children and their father.

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner was not married to the children's father during the years at issue
findings_of_fact.snippet: She was not married to her children's father during the years at issue.

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner paid most of the household expenses each year
findings_of_fact.snippet: She paid most of the household expenses for each year at issue but filed as head of household for only 2015 and 2016.

findings_of_fact.fact: Children's father did not claim the children and did not file as head of household for 2015 and 2016; petitioner had the greater AGI
findings_of_fact.snippet: The children's father did not claim the three children as his dependents for the years at issue

findings_of_fact.fact: Respondent conceded two of the three children are qualifying children for each year
findings_of_fact.snippet: He has also conceded that petitioner is entitled to claim two of her three children as qualifying child dependents

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner was a student in 2013 and paid tuition that year; no evidence of tuition paid in 2014
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner was a student in 2013 and paid tuition in that year, but there is no evidence that she paid tuition in 2014.

issues.question: Is petitioner entitled to head of household filing status for 2015 and 2016?
issues.holding: Yes; unmarried, maintained a household with qualifying children for more than half the year, and furnished over half the cost of maintaining it
issues.computable_reason: Follows mechanically from found facts (unmarried, qualifying children in household, over half of household cost) under §2(b)

issues.question: Is petitioner entitled to a $1,000 education credit for 2014?
issues.holding: No; she did not establish payment of tuition in 2014
issues.computable_reason: Decided on failure to substantiate tuition payment in 2014

decision.text: Decision will be entered under Rule 155.
decision.summary: Head of household allowed for 2015 and 2016; 2014 education credit disallowed; penalties conceded by respondent

notes: Very short opinion; HOH findings are general ('paid most of the household expenses'), no dollar figures for household costs. Months of residence of children not stated numerically; court treats membership for more than half the year as found.
